pr_title: [8.x] Add a cluster listener to fix missing system index mappings after upgrade
pr_body:
This PR modifies `TransportVersionsFixupListener` to include all of compatibility versions (not only TransportVersion) in the fixup.

`TransportVersionsFixupListener` spots the instances when the master has been upgraded to the most recent code version, along with non-master nodes, but some nodes are missing a "proper" (non-inferred) Transport version.
This PR adds another check to also ensure that we have real (non-empty) system index mapping versions.

To do so, it modifies NodeInfo so it carries all of CompatibilityVersions (TransportVersion + SystemIndexDescriptor.MappingVersions).

This was initially done via a separate fixup listener + ad-hoc transport action, but the 2 listeners "raced" to update ClusterState on the same CompatibilityVersions structure; it just made sense to do it at the same time.

The fixup is very similar to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110710, which does the same for cluster features; plus, it adds a CI test to cover the bug raised in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112694

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112694

```
          "hash": -1434574148

```

hi, @thecoop, this bug will result in mappings_versions map empty, It will lead creating system indices error. It's a serious problem.  Is there any progress now?

After a first investigation, I think this is the specular of https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112946: in a mixed cluster situation, if a new (e.g. 8.15) node comes up, it can trigger the creation of a inference system indices. But that will be carried on by the master node; if the master is still on an older version (e.g. 8.9) its `SystemIndices` will not have any system index descriptor for the inference indices, and that's where the NPE comes from. 
I'll keep investigating to understand where/what/when the creation is triggered, so we can decide how to best prevent a "too early" creation of the indices.

- the inference API gets called on an upgraded node (8.9 does not have the endpoint)

If the `mappings_versions ` from command `GET _cluster/state` is empty, it will cause NPE.
I guess the bug is from the PR https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99114 And  https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99555

> If the mappings_versions from command GET _cluster/state is empty, it will cause NPE.

~~They are related, even if not directly~~. 
This is not strictly true: what appears in cluster state is the compatibility versions, which are derived from the system index descriptors, not vice-versa. SystemIndices could still have valid data even if `mappings_versions` is empty.
That said, an empty `mappings_versions` is a symptom that something is wrong, and neither should ever happen if the cluster is fully upgraded.
@weizijun do you have a case in which the cluster is fully upgraded (no nodes on 8.9 or any previous version) and this still happens?
If so, can you share logs of that cluster?

So, from my tests it seems that the mixed cluster scenario can be ruled out.
The transport action behind PUT inference (`TransportPutInferenceModelAction`) is also a master node action, and it was added in 8.11.
Which means it is not possible to invoke it on a cluster with 8.9 master node -- the transport service simply bails with a different error.

What we see in "mappings_versions" and what we read from `SystemIndices#findMatchingDescriptor` comes from the SystemIndexDescriptors declared by each plugin. 
If they are totally missing, like it seems to be from the output above, it might indicate a problem with loading them from plugins or parsing them.
@weizijun , @Huaixinww Logs from around node start of the master node would give use a better indication if there is a problem there.
Also knowing which plugins are installed would help.

@weizijun Did the upgraded cluster eventually resolve itself? By that I mean did the missing `mappings_versions` appear and were you able to create the Inference endpoint? We would like to know if the issue was transient or if the cluster ever recovered. Thank you

> Did the upgraded cluster eventually resolve itself? By that I mean did the missing `mappings_versions` appear and were you able to create the Inference endpoint? We would like to know if the issue was transient or if the cluster ever recovered. Thank you

The cluster will never recovery. It can't create the Inference endpoint because of the NPE of creating inference index. We will provide the logs of master to see what happen.

Just a head's up: I talked to @rjernst and the missing "mappings_versions" can be a red herring and unrelated to the NPE. 
Still, the rest stands: the descriptor in SystemIndices are declared statically (in code) by the plugin, and read during NodeConstruction, so if they are not present (which is why we have a NPE) something is probably going wrong on the master node. 
It's pretty important to have logs especially from the early phases (node start), as SystemIndices is created at start and never changes.

Hi, @ldematte , I noticed that, our version upgrade process is to add all new version nodes to the cluster,  all data transfer from old version nodes to new version nodes, and then shutdown all old nodes. I send the master log of new node to @davidkyle.

Hello @weizijun, I got the log file, thanks. 
Unfortunately it's very hard to work out what's going on without logs from all nodes tho (old and new), especially the master (from the logs, this is `es-cn-35t3xjo7a000190t2-data-i-1` initially, then `es-cn-35t3xjo7a000190t2-data-i-0` -- both ver 8.9 -- and then becomes `es-cn-35t3xjo7a000190t2-data-i2-2` -- ver 8.15.1).
One thing we need to understand is why the newly-started node (`es-cn-35t3xjo7a000190t2-data-i2-2`) becomes master straight away rather than joining an existing master.
Is your upgrade process doing something to force that? What else happens during your upgrade process? Allocation filtering, manual killing of nodes, or anything else?
Without complete logs for the whole cluster and a detailed description of what is happening/the actions performed on the cluster I'm afraid there is very little we can do.

I was able to reproduce it with the sequence described. 
Looks like we are missing a fixup: when the last 8.9 node leaves the cluster, the system indices descriptors/their mappings versions are not update to reflect what is now available to the cluster.
Restarting the master will force the update, but that should not be needed.
The issue has been fixed for 8.17 (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/115771) and is being backported to 8.16.1 too (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/116646)

Than you @ldematte for fixing and thank you @Huaixinww for reporting the bug.

Closing this issue as fixed 😄
